close_reason: Resolved 2026-05-10: removed tokio from [dependencies] in canonical jmap-mail-server and propagated to all 6 sibling extension-server crates (chat, calendars, contacts, tasks, filenode, sharing). Production code uses std::future::Future, never tokio types. Dev-deps still pull in tokio for #[tokio::test]. cargo test --workspace clean; cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings clean. Commit a6210dc.
description:
Cargo.toml:20 declares tokio = { workspace = true } as a regular dep. Cargo.toml:23 adds dev-deps tokio = { workspace = true, features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros"] }.

The library code itself uses tokio only in #[cfg(test)] modules (test_support module gates on #[cfg(test)], and #[tokio::test] is dev-only). Searching src/ for tokio:: returns no production-code uses. The only 'real' use is via the AFIT bound 'impl Future<Output = ...> + Send' which doesn't actually need tokio — that's a std future.

If the workspace tokio default features pull in any IO/runtime code, this crate is forcing every consumer to pay the binary cost of tokio just to consume the trait. Recommend:
1. Drop tokio from regular [dependencies], OR
2. Use tokio = { workspace = true, default-features = false } in regular deps if there is some reason to keep the dep (e.g. one of the bound types requires Send-compatible futures from tokio types).

Worth checking the workspace tokio definition:
    grep tokio /home/mark/PROJECT/JMAP/Cargo.toml

This is not a hot finding — workspace tokio is likely already minimal. P4/opinion. The same pattern probably exists in jmap-mail-server and could be coordinated.

Compile-time impact: dropping tokio from regular deps reduces type-resolution graph size for each consumer. Marginal but cumulative.
title: Cargo.toml: tokio is a runtime dep but only the no-default tokio is needed in lib code
